newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-KRYGIER STRIKES AS AMERICANS WIN OPENER.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-KRYGIER STRIKES AS AMERICANS WIN OPENER.

text.p: The United States needed a third-period goal from Washington Capital winger Todd Krygier to secure a 5-4 win over Latvia in their opening match at the world ice hockey championship on Sunday.
Krygier stalled a determined Latvian comeback bid with 6:23 remaining in the third when he picked up his own rebound and snapped a wristshot past Juris Klodans.

Until then the Americans had watched a 4-1 lead disappear as Latvia, playing in their first world championship since 1939, stormed back with three third-period goals from Leonids Tambijevs, Aleksandrs Belavakis and Andrei Ignatovics.
U.S. coach Jeff Jackson immediately called a time-out to calm his players, who then went out and swiftly scored the winner.
Vancouver Canuck enforcer Donald Brashear had opened scoring in the first period with a breakaway goal, only to have Sergei Cudinovs equalise 55 seconds later.
Brian Berard showed why he is the leading candidate to claim NHL rookie of the year honours when he scored a powerplay goal to put the U.S. back in front.
Taking control of the puck in the neutral zone, the New York Islander defenceman split two Latvian defenders before finishing with what might prove to be the most delightful goal of the tournament.
The Americans added two more goals in the second period from Hartford Whalers Paul Ranheim and Chris Tancill for their 4-1 lead.
